content: 1. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when combined with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if co-administration is unavoidable. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitor closely. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid P-gp inhibitors; the interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to decreased metabolism of toremifene. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of toremifene with QT-prolonging agents should be avoided. If co-administration is required, interrupt toremifene therapy or closely monitor the patient for QT prolongation. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. Monitor closely. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Both trazodone and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Both clarithromycin and triclabendazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Both trifluoperazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Both clarithromycin and trimethoprim prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Both clarithromycin and tropisetron prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 19. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. 20. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the live bacterial vaccine. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 24. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Monitor closely for QTc interval prolongation. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Both clarithromycin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Both clarithromycin and vorinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 36. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with clarithromycin 250 mg twice daily, or to 80 mg once daily with clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing clarithromycin. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zavegepant intranasal by inhibiting OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of zidovudine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
